# Colour

**Foundation group:** visual elements  
**Reviewed against:** GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 on 2026-09-09

Use GOV.UK functional colours and the refreshed palette to keep meaning, interaction states and contrast consistent across services.

## Rules

- Always start from the current GOV.UK palette and use functional colours for essential page elements.
- In Sass use govuk-functional-colour with a purpose such as brand, text, link, focus, error or success instead of copying a hexadecimal value.
- In plain CSS use the corresponding functional custom-property alias from tokens/govuk.css; palette variables are for reviewed mappings, not new semantics.
- Preserve the full hover, visited, active, error, success and focus state system when adapting components.
- Update the pinned token set when GOV.UK Frontend changes instead of retaining an obsolete colour for visual compatibility.

## Accessibility contract

- Text and interactive elements must meet WCAG 2.2 level AA contrast requirements in every state.
- Never use colour as the only way to communicate status, validation, selection or action hierarchy.
- Test custom colour combinations rather than assuming that two palette colours have sufficient contrast.
- Retain the yellow focus background and dark focus text unless official component guidance specifies another tested treatment.

## Restrictions and caveats

- Do not assign a new meaning to an existing GOV.UK functional colour.
- Do not claim an interface is GOV.UK-conformant because its brand blue and green values match the palette.
- This portable token export does not replace GOV.UK Frontend component CSS.

## Token references

- `govuk.color.brand`
- `govuk.color.text`
- `govuk.color.secondary-text`
- `govuk.color.link`
- `govuk.color.link-visited`

## Examples

### Functional colour in plain CSS

```css
.app-status--error {
  color: var(--govuk-error-colour);
  border-left: var(--govuk-border-width) solid currentcolor;
}
```
